transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. That's considered light exercise, which is fine to do.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure whether it's safe to use yours specifically, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team to confirm.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long ago your surgery was. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay. 

How long ago was your operation?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago. I'll keep an eye on it, but thank you for the information. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to know. A week is still early days, so some blurriness is normal at this stage. It should continue to improve over the coming days and weeks.

Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you for answering all my questions. I appreciate the help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass
